For the last eight months, I’ve also had these odd sensations, like something is crawling on my arms or tapping my shoulder when no one is there. I’ve started to worry that someone in the department—or higher up—is monitoring me, maybe tracking my computer or bugging my office. Sometimes I catch myself using words that I know aren’t real, like “textual shimmerlines” or “mind-static,” but they make perfect sense to me at the time.

More recently, maybe three months, I’ve pulled back from friends and colleagues. I avoid faculty gatherings and barely return calls. I lie in bed thinking it might be easier if I just didn’t wake up, not that I’d do anything, but there’s this recurring wish to just stop existing. It’s making it harder to teach and to be present with my family.

It’s like I’ve had this motor in me that doesn’t shut off. I pace around the stacks, start three or four projects at once, then can’t actually finish anything because my mind keeps jumping. For about eight months I’ve also been convinced there’s something seriously wrong inside my body—like my organs are decaying or rearranging themselves. Doctors say all the tests are fine, but I can feel it. Sometimes, especially when I’m keyed up, I see shapes or figures in the corners of the aisles, people standing between the shelves, and when I look straight at them, they’re gone. I can’t tell if it’s just my head playing tricks on me, but it keeps happening.

D006-D010_h025.question_both:
I guess this all really started about a year ago. I went from being my usual, pretty driven self to feeling like I was on overdrive all the time. On the road for work, I’d be buzzing, talking nonstop to doctors, setting up extra calls, starting side projects at 2 or 3 a.m. and not feeling tired at all. I’d sleep maybe two, three hours and still feel wired, almost “too good.” I was suddenly super outgoing, messaging old classmates, going out with clients after hours, flirting, driving way too fast between hospitals, like the rules didn’t really apply to me.

Around nine months ago, I also started getting these strange body things. I’m convinced something’s wrong inside me—like my organs are decaying or infected—even though my tests keep coming back normal. Sometimes it feels like bugs are crawling under my skin or something’s brushing against me when nothing’s there. It freaks me out, but I also catch myself talking in this sing-songy, rhyming way—“skin, spin, thin”—and my husband tells me I’m not making sense.

Lately, I’ve crashed. For about six months now I’ve been crying at random, barely hungry, moving like I’m underwater. I lie in bed for hours unable to fall asleep, then drag myself around the next day. I used to love meeting doctors and coworkers; now I mostly avoid people, even friends. My numbers at work have dropped, and at home I just sit there, staring, while my husband tries to get me to talk.
D006-D010_h025.question_a:
It started about a year ago. I got into this…high. I felt amazing, like I was on top of my territory and could easily double my numbers. I barely slept—maybe two, three hours—and I didn’t feel tired. I’d get up, map out four hospitals before breakfast, then decide to “network” at random bars after, talking nonstop to strangers, doctors, reps, anyone. I was driving way too fast between calls, cutting corners, not really caring if I got a ticket or worse. My husband kept telling me to slow down, but I just felt too wired and “right.”

Around nine months ago, on top of that, I became convinced something was wrong inside my body—like my organs were decaying, even though all my labs were normal. Sometimes I feel things crawling under my skin or little taps on my arms when nothing is there. My words can get away from me—“sales, sails, tales, rails”—I catch myself rhyming instead of making sense.

For a couple of those months, the body worries and the skin sensations kept going even after the high burned out. I wasn’t up, just flat and withdrawn, barely talking to friends or coworkers. Then about six months ago I crashed—crying at random in my car, no appetite, lying in bed moving so slowly it felt like walking through mud, staring at the ceiling for hours before I could even fall asleep. I’ve been missing work and my performance has tanked.
D006-D010_h025.question_b:
It’s been about a year now where I’ve been “stuck on high,” I guess. I feel wired and amazing most of the time, like I’m invincible. I barely sleep—maybe two or three hours—and I’m still up at 5 a.m. planning new client routes, new marketing ideas, cleaning the house, messaging coworkers, old classmates, even doctors from my territory. I’ll drive way too fast between appointments, cut people off, and only afterwards think, “That could’ve gone really bad.” My husband says I talk nonstop and jump from one thing to another.

When I’m in these high phases, I also get convinced something’s wrong inside my body—that my organs are rotting or my blood is poisoned—so I keep asking doctors in my territory to “just run one more panel.” I sometimes feel things crawling under my skin or little electric zaps on my arms when nothing’s there. My words start coming out in rhymes without me meaning to—“heart, chart, start, smart”—and it’s hard to stay on track.  

When the “high” drops, like for the past six months off and on, I slow to a crawl. I cry easily, my appetite basically disappears, and it takes forever to fall asleep even though I’m exhausted. Walking into a clinic feels like wading through mud. I’ve stopped seeing friends and even avoid company dinners.  

The weird body beliefs and skin sensations only happen when I’m in that revved‑up, euphoric state; they don’t stick around when my mood crashes.
